package_info.why_malicious: These four versions of the Ultralytics package were compromised to include malicious code that performed unauthorized cryptocurrency mining. The attack leveraged weaknesses in the CI/CD pipeline and compromised API tokens to inject and distribute the malicious code to users.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code downloads a shell script from a remote server and executes it, which installs and runs a cryptocurrency miner on the victim's machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Import-time execution of remote code is highly unusual and dangerous, especially when it downloads and runs a shell script from an untrusted domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not execute remote code or install additional software upon import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated update checkers or telemetry (with user consent) may contact remote servers, but should never execute arbitrary code.
key_indicators: os.system call with remote script execution
curl command fetching from non-official domain
execution of shell script at import-time

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code launches a cryptocurrency mining process using a bundled or downloaded miner binary, connecting to a mining pool with a hardcoded wallet address.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Launching a cryptocurrency miner as part of a package's runtime behavior is a clear abuse of user resources and is not expected in any legitimate package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not mine cryptocurrency or launch hidden processes unrelated to their advertised functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; mining cryptocurrency on user machines without consent is always malicious.
key_indicators: hardcoded mining pool and wallet address

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into the package during the build process via compromised CI/CD or API token.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious package is published to PyPI.

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the compromised Ultralytics package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes on user machine.

attack_chain.action: At import-time, the package downloads and executes a remote shell script to install a cryptocurrency miner.
attack_chain.leads_to: Miner is installed and ready to run.

attack_chain.action: At runtime, the miner process is launched, connecting to a mining pool and using the victim's resources for unauthorized mining.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives mined cryptocurrency; victim's resources are abused.

behavioral_signatures: Import-time or install-time execution of remote shell scripts
Runtime launching of cryptocurrency mining processes
Network connections to known mining pools from package code
file_indicators: Unexpected shell scripts downloaded and executed
Presence of miner binaries (e.g., xmrig) in package directories
Modifications to __init__.py or other entry-point files to include os.system or subprocess calls
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to non-official domains during import or install
Connections to known mining pool domains or IPs (e.g., pool.example.com:3333)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that execute os.system or subprocess calls with remote URLs or mining software. Flag packages that download and execute shell scripts at import or install time. Detect unexpected network connections to mining pools or suspicious domains from Python processes. Review package contents for embedded or downloaded miner binaries.
